normative_candidate.heard_prefix: The exactly measured portion of assistant output demonstrably played to/heard by the user remains eligible for ephemeral next-turn dialogue context.
normative_candidate.unheard_tail: Assistant semantics beyond the measured heard/playout boundary are excluded from next-turn authoritative dialogue context.
normative_candidate.durable_memory: Interrupted output does not become durable canonical memory merely because a heard prefix is retained ephemerally. Durable admission remains independently gated.
normative_candidate.effects_and_tools: Cancelled or stale generation outputs/tool results cannot regain authority after cancellation unless a separate current causal owner explicitly admits them.
normative_candidate.commit_eligibility: Existing VoiceOutputPacket commit_eligible semantics remain unchanged: only fully heard completed output may be commit eligible.
normative_candidate.measurement_binding: The retained boundary must be bound to a playout/heard measurement identity, not inferred from generated audio length or response.done alone.

current_f2_source_facts.fact: VoiceOutputPacket requires playback_state=completed and heard_fraction=1.0 for commit_eligible=true; interrupted output can retain a monotone heard_fraction while remaining non-commit-eligible.
Current F2 authority distinguishes durable commit eligibility from ephemeral next-turn conversational context and leaves the latter policy unresolved.

external_primary_evidence.finding: Realtime interruption handling updates history so server-side conversation stays aligned with what the user actually heard; delayed playback should use playback tracking so truncation follows actual playback position.
On interruption, assistant audio/history is truncated to what the user actually heard; local history follows the corresponding truncation/conversation events.
LiveKit interruption handling automatically truncates conversation history to include only the portion of agent speech the user heard before interruption.

reasoning_summary.compatibility: Two independent current realtime voice stacks converge on heard-prefix history retention rather than whole-response amnesia.
reasoning_summary.dialogue_coherence: Keeping exactly what the user heard preserves common conversational reference while deleting the unheard tail prevents the model from relying on words the user never received.
reasoning_summary.authority_separation: Ephemeral next-turn context can preserve dialogue continuity without granting durable memory, VoiceOutcome, effect, training, or whole-product credit.
reasoning_summary.falsifiability: The policy yields a direct runtime oracle: heard prefix present + unheard tail absent is the semantic match; prefix amnesia or tail leakage are distinct failures after canonical policy adoption.

counterhypothesis.note: Whole-response deletion remains a possible explicit product choice, but current external primary behavior and dialogue-continuity considerations do not support treating it as the compatibility default.

trigger4_handoff.requested_action: Pin an explicit F2 interrupted-response next-turn context policy through normal Trigger4/F2 mutation authority, preferably this candidate. Do not alter durable memory/effect authority and do not create a second context authority.
trigger4_handoff.after_pin: Execute the existing HF09/HF10 protocol-compatibility lane through the already-proven controller -> vps-clay-host route; do not duplicate dispatch.

next_exact_action: Trigger4/F2 authority explicitly pins the interrupted-response context policy without changing durable commit semantics, then the existing HF09/HF10 lane measures exact heard-prefix retention versus tail leakage on the proven VPS controller route.
